Composition: wide, moderate-distance eye-level camera from BEHIND the people on an ordinary old cobbled lane outside a modest brewery entrance. A narrow open earth trench crosses the lower foreground diagonally, clearly exposing a long dull brown wooden water pipe made from bored timber/log sections at its bottom, a plausible period material interpretation. Simple Georgian brick facades with sash windows and two plain stone gate pillars form the background. Cool overcast spring daylight.
People: exactly FOUR generic fictional adult men: one anonymous middle-aged brewery worker/master on the left in a plain dark long coat, knee breeches, wool stockings and period leather shoes, NO wig, short plain greying hair seen ONLY from the back; and three municipal workmen on the right in plain worn linen/wool work coats or smocks, knee breeches, stockings and simple brimmed hats. EVERY person is fully REAR-facing, all necks and heads averted away from camera, absolutely no cheek profiles, eyes, facial features or recognizable likenesses. All are looking toward the trench or brewery gate. Their figures fit fully in the wider scene with space around them.
Tool and action: the brewery man calmly holds the plain WOODEN shaft of a work pickaxe at waist level with one relaxed hand, while the dark wrought-IRON pick head rests firmly ON THE GROUND beside his feet. The iron tool is low and inactive, not raised, swung, pointed, aimed or brandished at anyone. Other workmen have simple shovels lowered with blades resting on the earth and plain cloth sacks nearby. They have paused their work, with a few feet of calm open space between them. No touching, physical aggression, fighting, chase, intimidation pose, shouting gesture, or weapon threat.
